title: Microfeature probe catalog + customer vignettes (sep 2029)
content:
Purpose: quick catalog of small, testable feature probes derived from recent customer conversations + short customer vignettes to help engineering/product pick low-risk, high-learning experiments.

Context and why this doc: lots of asks that are not full features but would materially reduce friction (per-route token caps, safer fallback UX, cheaper inference knobs). We want a lean list of experiments we can run in the next 6–10 weeks to validate impact and operator effort. This lives as a working note — rough scoring, unresolved questions, quotes from customers.

Synthesis highlights (top themes across 18 calls / 24 tickets):
- Cost surprise: customers report unpredictable per-session costs when prompts vary; ask: better per-route visibility + soft caps.
- Degradation handling: several customers (enterprise) want graceful fallback to cheaper model variants when latency spikes rather than 5xx errors.
- Quality regressions: teams want easy A/B compare + per-prompt eval hooks during rollouts.
- Ops friction: manual tuning of batching/kv cache for mixed workloads. Small UI toggles or autosuggest could remove 2–3 weekly SRE interventions.

Microfeature probes (short descriptions, hypothesized impact, quick effort estimate):
1) Per-route soft token cap + warning signal
   - What: allow customers to set a soft token budget on a route that shows a pre-flight warning and produces a cheap summary instead of full generation once exceeded.
   - Hypothesis: reduces bill surprises and support tickets; increases stickiness for customers with bursty prompts.
   - Success metric: 20% drop in "unexpected-usage" tickets for pilot customers in 30 days.
   - Effort: M (2 wks front-end + 1 wk backend + 1 infra config)

2) Auto-fallback policy: latency-first model cascade
   - What: policy that routes to smaller quantized variants when p90 latency exceeds threshold, with telemetry flagging.
   - Hypothesis: keeps sessions alive, reduces error rates during noisy infra events.
   - Success metric: reduce session error rate from spikes by 60% in pilot region.
   - Effort: H (3 weeks + can leverage existing routing hooks)

3) Rollout attach points: per-prompt labeled eval collector
   - What: lightweight SDK hook that records prompt+response for rollout groups (opt-in, PII-filtered) and provides per-prompt quality diffs in Console.
   - Hypothesis: Faster detection of regressions, fewer rollbacks.
   - Success metric: time-to-detect-regression reduced from days to hours for canaries.
   - Effort: M (2–3 weeks)

4) Batching autosuggest: workload-aware batch size recommendation
   - What: Console will analyze recent traffic patterns and suggest batch sizes/latency tradeoffs per model/route.
   - Hypothesis: reduces manual SRE tuning and lowers token cost per response by 5–15%.
   - Success metric: 10% average unit-cost reduction for customers who adopted suggestions.
   - Effort: M (2 weeks analysis + UI)

5) Cheap-summary fallback mode (response-level degradation)
  - What: when tokens or latency exceed thresholds, system returns a concise summary or bullet list instead of full generation; customers can opt in per-route.
  - Hypothesis: preserves UX while bounding cost/latency.
  - Success metric: satisfaction score in pilot >= 70%; reduced timeouts.
  - Effort: L–M (1–2 weeks)

Customer vignettes (short, anonymized):
- "Legal tech startup" (mid-market, sec): "We ran a long search prompt and suddenly the bill blew up. We need a way to say 'stop at 800 tokens' or at least something that warns me before it exceeds budget."
  -> Notes: willing to trial soft caps if Console shows per-route burn.

- "Ecommerce personalization team" (scale startup): "During holiday load we had timeouts. We'd rather get a shorter answer than a hard failure."
  -> Notes: receptive to cheap-summary fallback and auto-fallback routing.

- "Health data integrator" (enterprise, private deployment): "We can't stream raw prompts to a third party for evals, but we'd pay for a built-in labeled-eval hook that anonymizes and stores metrics."
  -> Notes: requires opt-in and strong PII filters; potential upsell for Private offering.

Prioritization matrix (quick, conservative scoring):
- Criteria: customer pain (0–5), implement effort (0–5, inverted), revenue/expansion signal (0–5), operational risk (0–5, inverted).
- Per-route soft token cap: pain 4, effort 3, rev 3, risk 4 -> weighted suggests medium-high priority.
- Auto-fallback policy: pain 5, effort 4, rev 4, risk 3 -> high priority for availability-focused customers.
- Rollout eval collector: pain 3, effort 3, rev 5, risk 2 -> high priority for product teams.
- Batching autosuggest: pain 3, effort 3, rev 2, risk 4 -> medium priority.
- Cheap-summary fallback: pain 4, effort 2, rev 2, risk 4 -> low-medium (fast win).

Experiment designs (minimal viable experiment for each):
- Soft token cap: pick 3 pilot customers (two mid-market, one startup), create per-route config in Console flagged as "soft-cap"; observe tickets and retention over 30 days; add in-UI pre-send modal when threshold approached.
- Auto-fallback: enable for single region for customers with bursty traffic; use existing routing rules to insert cheaper variant. Add telemetry tag to measure session continuity and error rates.
- Rollout eval: release SDK opt-in to 5 internal product teams first, gather labeled diffs, feed into Console visualization.

Implementation risks & mitigations:
- PII/Compliance: any prompt capture must be opt-in and pass PII scrubber; for Private customers consider local-only eval sinks.
- Behavioral change: cheap-summary may reduce perceived product value; add A/B to measure retention/engagement.
- Capacity interplay: auto-fallback might increase load on smaller pools; need throttles and cost guardrails.

Open questions for engineering/product:
- Can routing layer already express the exact cascading semantics we need or does it require kernel changes? (ask infra/serving-runtime)
- What is the minimum privacy scrub needed to ship rollout eval safely for enterprise? (ask security/compliance)
- Quick UI mocks: who can spin a Console modal prototype for soft-caps? (ask DX)

Next actions (owner & ETA):
- Align infra feasibility: Liaise with Serving Runtime (owner: Devon Park) by 2029-09-20.
- Legal/compliance check on eval capture requirements (owner: Sana Rahman) by 2029-09-22.
- Prototype Console pre-send warning for soft token cap (owner: Liam O'Connor) by 2029-09-28.
- Recruit 3 pilot customers and prepare communication template (owner: Maya Thompson) by 2029-10-01.

Notes to self / loose fragments:
- Could tie soft-caps to billing alerts and recommended plan suggestions.
- Consider 'graceful degrade' flag in SDK so apps can decide whether to accept short summaries.
- Add a small telemetry tag to mark 'microfeature pilot' flows to avoid skewing global metrics.

Appendix: raw snippets from calls (anonymized)
- "...we lost trust after one month where two big sessions maxed out and the invoice doubled"
- "...if there was an option to return a TL;DR, our customers would prefer that over a failure"
- "...our security team won't allow sending production prompts to vendors, but we can test on synthetic prompts"

—— end of working note —–
Feedback welcome — this is intentionally rough. Please add customer leads or links to tickets in linked_artifacts if you want a specific ask added to the pilot list.
